kjv: then let him write her a bill of divorcement
mine: and he writes her a certificate of divorce
note: Verses 1-3 are a single chain of "if" clauses (ki ... wekhatav ... weshillechah) describing the case, and the only command is in v. 4 (no remarriage to the first husband); the KJV makes v. 1 an instruction to divorce, the reading the Pharisees press in Matt 19:7 ("Moses commanded").
Hebrew 'erwat davar ("nakedness of a thing") is vague and was famously debated (Hillel vs. Shammai); it suggests something shameful or improper, not ritual uncleanness.

kjv: she may go and be another man's [wife]
mine: and goes and becomes another man's wife
note: The verbs continue the protasis; the KJV's "may" turns a description into a permission.
Hebrew hit'ammer (as in 21:14) means to treat as a chattel, exploit; selling is mentioned separately.

mine: a case of a skin disease
note: Hebrew tsara'at covers a range of skin conditions (and mould on fabric and walls), not Hansen's disease specifically.
